2. The prayer in the writ petition is made for direction upon the respondents to forthwith take all due and effective remedial measures for proper Rehabilitation & Resettlement of the petitioners and those being affected from the acquisition of villages Jugra, Arahara and Chepakalan in terms with the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
3. Mr. Rohit Ranjan Sinha, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners through Video Conferencing submits that the notifications were issued under the signature of Deputy Secretary,
Department of Revenue and Land Reforms, Government of Jharkhand in terms with Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and in terms with Section 3 of the Land Acquisition (Mines) Act,
1885 for the the villages namely Chepakalan, Arhara Jgra and the lands were acquired however no measures have been taken for rehabilitation of the villagers of that villages since 2007, details of the plots have been disclosed in several paragraphs of the writ petition.

He further submits that the petitioners have already moved before the respondent-Deputy Commissioner, Hazaribagh as well as Union of India through Ministry of Coal and Power however, no measure has been taken to rehabilitate the said villagers.
4. Learned counsels for the State and NTPC jointly submit that the petitioners have alternative remedy and the matter can be referred to the tribunal in the light of the said Act.

5. In view of above this petition is being disposed of directing the Deputy Commissioner,
Hazaribagh to consider the representation of the petitioners in view of the averments made in the writ petition and treat this writ petition as representation in accordance with law within four weeks from the date of receipt/production of a copy of this order 6.
This writ petition is disposed of.
Pending I.A, if any, stands disposed of.

( Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi, J.) Satyarthi/
